read_scope.notes: Read the complete frozen 22-page PDF, including references and Appendices A-G; visually inspected all 22 rendered pages, Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-12. Read paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve notation, structure and source locations. Appendix derivations were read as optional technical depth rather than prerequisites for the main story. Used only the fixed rubric and supplied snapshot; independently verified the PDF SHA256 with shasum and Python hashlib. Extraction and rendering used an isolated /tmp/editorial_r25_b_v8d20mjt directory.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise scientific English with manageable sentences and stable distinctions among shared change, aligned response and total error. Sections 4.1 and 5.4 explain difficult ideas in ordinary language before interpreting numbers. Qualifications generally identify their actual consequence rather than merely disclaiming validity. A small amount of duplication between the Section 3.3 feature inventory and Table 1 is the main economical editing opportunity.
score_reasons.structure: The main text progresses coherently from the Monet/Sisley motivation through the controlled clauses, feature representation, intuitive score examples, inference, primary findings and retrospective explanations. The Results headings communicate findings, and source correction explicitly revisits the original statistical comparisons. Detailed identities, control simulations, distribution summaries and historical interventions are successfully kept in optional appendices. No consequential structural gap is apparent; remaining editing is localized.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The lightness example and the no-distinction/exact/doubled-response example make centering and the D benchmark unusually accessible. The design counts, reference collection, scaling units, controls and calibration operation can be understood without the repository. Figure captions explain symbols and numerical benchmarks; Table 4 makes the scene-averaging and calibration distinctions concrete. The abstract is standalone overall, but its benchmark sentence could state more directly that uncertainty prevents establishing an advantage, since the lowest point estimate is actually below one.
score_reasons.engagement: The opening poses a consequential, concrete evaluation problem, and the paper sustains it through interpretable counterexamples: nearly unit alignment with substantial error, weak Monet/Sisley responses, and changes in model ordering after scene averaging or calibration. Figure 1 invites direct comparison of all six prompt conditions; Figure 2 magnifies the close painter means; Figure 3 reveals uneven pair responses at a glance. Brief streamlining of the duplicated feature inventory would improve the pace before the central comparison.

strengths: Section 4.1, p. 5, uses an actual Monet-Sisley lightness gap and three idealized D values (1, 0, 1) to establish intuition before indexed equations.

Sections 3.1-3.3, pp. 2-3, identify the finite digital reference target, equal painter weighting, separate development scaling and identical scene clauses without implying matched historical compositions or perceptual validation.

Figure 1, p. 4, visibly shows the named conditions and both controls; its caption states that the reference reproductions were neither inputs nor composition matches and identifies the example-selection rule.
Figures 2-3, pp. 7-8, provide complementary projected geometry and full-feature pair scores, with readable detail views, color keys and explicit meanings for zero, one and negative estimates.

Section 5.4 and Table 4, p. 9, explain why scene averaging and scaling can change the lowest error estimate, while making clear that calibration changes feature contrasts and does not improve images or establish statistical superiority.

Section 5.5 and Table 5, pp. 9-10, make the changed Sunburst, Flare and GPT Image 1 comparisons explicit after source correction and preserve the distinction between original inference and retrospective sensitivity.

The manuscript consistently distinguishes numerical agreement from perceived resemblance, discloses the AI-only source audit and incomplete exact-pixel access, and keeps historical supporting cohorts separate from the current experiment.

findings.issue: The phrase "none demonstrates lower total error" is defensible but leaves an abstract-only reader to infer that the obstacle is uncertainty. FLUX has an error point estimate below the no-distinction benchmark, as Section 5.1 explains, so the abstract could make that distinction more immediate.
findings.reader_effect: A reader scanning only the abstract could mistake lack of established superiority for an observation that every estimated error is at least the benchmark.
findings.suggested_change: Replace "yet none demonstrates lower total error than a predictor making no painter distinctions" with "but uncertainty prevents establishing lower error than a predictor making no painter distinctions". This preserves the statistical claim and the existing 155-word abstract length.

findings.location: Section 3.3 and Table 1, p. 3; paper.tex lines 157-169 and 177-186
findings.issue: The opening paragraph enumerates the color, spatial and texture families in prose, and the immediately adjacent table repeats most of that inventory with interpretations. The subsequent chroma and contrast examples do more distinct explanatory work.
findings.reader_effect: The reader encounters the same feature taxonomy twice before reaching the central comparison, slightly slowing an otherwise well-paced introduction to the methods.
findings.suggested_change: Shorten the first three family-description sentences to a table-directed overview, retaining the concrete chroma/contrast examples and the metric limitation. Preserve the named methods and their citations in Table 1 or the existing Appendix A definitions. This is a cut or relocation within the current 22 pages, not a request for additional material.

summary: Excellent editorial communication of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The main question, intervention, two scores and principal findings are readily understood, and the paper handles retrospective calibration, uncertain rankings and source sensitivity with care. Only localized clarification and streamlining are warranted; no new experiment, perceptual validation or expansion is needed.
